sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: An aquatic or semi-aquatic perennial reaching about 1 m, rooted in mud or shallow water along ponds, ditches and slow-flowing streams. Leaves form a basal clump; a tall stalk bears a branched, whorled panicle of small three-petalled white to pink flowers. Despite its common name, it is not a member of the genus Plantago.

sections.title: Food and toxicity
sections.text: Its starchy rhizome has been eaten in some regions, but Kew warns that ingestion in large quantities is poisonous. It should not be presented simply as a food plant.
